pageCache.text:
Creative and Performing Arts
Ashford School prides itself on ‘Celebrating Individuality’ and we strive for Creative and Performing Arts to be an integral cog in the educational lives and development of all our pupils.
Music
The active and exciting musical life of Ashford School centres on Brake Hall and its environs, which include The Octagons (two octagon-shaped rehearsal and classroom spaces) and a number of individual and larger classrooms for our one-on-one and year group lessons.
Music is not only an integral part of the curriculum at Ashford School, but is also a subject that bleeds into the co-curricular life of our students. Opportunities for performance are second-to-none, with a full programme of concerts, recitals and other events taking place throughout the year, in close co-operation with Ashford Prep School’s musical team. Also on offer are a number of after-school clubs and bands, ranging from Jazz and Electric bands to a full Orchestra and talented choir. Our instrumental team also provide tuition in all orchestra instruments (with the exception of harp), in addition to guitar (classical, electric and bass), piano and voice.
Each year the Music Department collaborates on both Junior and Senior dramatic productions. In March 2020, the School performed the acclaimed production of Beauty and the Beast with a large cast and a 15-piece Pit Band, most of whom were School musicians.
The very best instruments push students to new levels of success and our Senior School is home to some of the world’s best pianos.
Go to a famous concert hall and you are likely to see to the top performers playing on a Steinway piano. In 2013 we became an all-Steinway School, making us one of only 25 schools in the UK with Steinway-only pianos.
Drama
Drama at Ashford School goes beyond a simple skit and learning a few lines. We aim to instil a love and passion for the subject by immersing our students in opportunities to excel in all aspects of the subject, be it acting and singing, or make-up, lighting and special effects.
Key Stage 3 pupils spend each half term studying a new drama skill. These skills are discovered and built upon, term on term in order to improve and lead towards GCSE. Students learn about physical and vocals skills within various themes such as Shakespeare, improvisation, Commedia Dell Arte and many more.
GSCE and A Level students learn how to devise from a given stimulus and how to complete a written journal or analytical research report. Their skills of bringing characters to life are enhanced by learning lines and exploring practical rehearsal techniques from differing practitioners.
Students dive even deeper into the dramatic world by studying and analysing a variety of plays and set texts. By practically exploring the subject, they are required to bring the text to life through acting, sound effects, lighting effects and special effects.
Whether studying Drama as a chosen subject or just showing a love for acting, all students have extensive opportunities to develop their skills and interests in the dramatic arena through the variety of co-curricular activities on offer.
The School produces and performs three large-scale productions annually, which include two Junior Drama productions and one full-blown musical production by our Senior students. Produced by our Head of Drama, the productions involve our students from start to finish, including in aspects such as costume design and creation, choreography, lighting and props. Here, the students are able to put to use all they have learnt in class, but also all of the co-curricular skills they have developed during the co-curricular activities, such as Junior Drama Club and the Technical Club.
High achievers have the opportunity to take part in producing and directing their own showcases, and our A level students provide mentorship for aspiring dramatists at our annual primary school workshops. Students also regularly participate in festivals and competitions, with recent success obtained at the Kent and Hastings Festivals. A number of our students have also recently auditioned with the National Theatre.
The School welcomes a number of professional practitioners throughout the year, including the Frantic Assembly Physical Theatre Company and the Stanislavski Experience. Our Drama students enjoy a number of theatre trips throughout the year too, with recent trips to see Everybody’s Talking about Jamie and War Horse.
Ashford School employs a full-time Speech and Drama teacher and trains a number of Prep and Senior students each year to participate in the LAMDA exams.
We currently have 49 students across the Prep and Senior school taking LAMDA Acting, Verse and Prose and Public Speaking Exams.
Art
In order to be truly creative, students need to feel safe in their environment. They need to be allowed to make mistakes; they need to be taught the rules and then be free to break the rules. Only then can we truly teach our students to be exceptionally creative. At Ashford School, our Art department trains pupils from Year 7 upwards to think independently and to be freely creative, therefore developing key skills that students need for their future at university and beyond.
Take a tour around our virtual gallery via Artsteps.
The aim for the department is that, whilst teaching the fundamental skills of drawing and old master painting techniques, we remain highly innovative and contemporary, offering various forms of new media, including green screen, full Adobe Creative Suite, film and animation. Our Art department is acknowledged as one of the very best because it encourages all students to step outside their comfort zone and be adventurous learners in a truly supportive environment. All students are taught the fundamental skills of observational drawing as well as experimenting with a huge array of artistic media – from digital imaging software for green screens, to ceramics, intaglio printing, reduction block printing, screen printing, various forms of textile techniques, dark room and digital photography.
At GCSE, our students participate in workshops that focus on many of the above media. Students are then free to specialise within their chosen areas in year 11. At A level, students learn on a foundation-style course, studying all mediums, under the guidance of three qualified teachers, before being allowed to focus their practise in Year 13.
The art department and its students benefit from a fantastic full-time Art technician, who is on hand to help and enable ambitious and unusual projects come to life. More recently, these projects have included a mirrored maze exam piece that included sound.
The department also regularly organises student trips to London and surrounding areas for the lower years. Recent GCSE and A Level trips have included residential art tours to Edinburgh, Rome, Venice, Madrid and Berlin.
Outside of the classroom, students have the opportunity to participate in a large variety of art-focussed co-curricular clubs, including photography, animation and pottery. The School’s own Artist in Residence is also on-hand, allowing the students to talk to and work alongside a professional artist. In recent years, our students have worked alongside and exhibited with an animator, an installation artist and a photographer.
The students also benefit from the experience body of Art staff, who are all highly specialised and are artists within their own right. In recent years, the department staff have showcased their work at their own exhibition to allow students and parents to see their teacher’s passion for the subject.

Drama
Drama at Ashford School goes beyond a simple skit and learning a few lines. We aim to instil a love and passion for the subject by immersing our students in opportunities to excel in all aspects of the subject, be it acting and singing, or make-up, lighting and special effects.
The Year 7 Drama curriculum in broken into three main areas of explorative work. In the winter term, pupils develop their collaborative and creativity skills through the exploration of basic stagecraft and theatrical conventions. The key performance skills covered are physicality, movement, and the effective use of stage space. In the spring term, pupils build on their previous learning by exploring extracts of an established play text, encouraging them to consider how extracts might be staged to create mood and atmosphere, or to communicate a specific theme or genre. The key performance skills covered are the dynamic use of voice and speech, and characterisation. In the summer term, pupils explore the works of Keith Johnston, the renowned improvisation practitioner. Through the practical application of his teaching, pupils develop their problem-solving skills, adaptability, listening and responding skills, as well as their comedic timing and their ability to work with an audience. The key performance skills covered are the dynamic use of movement and gesture, and the exploration of proxemics.
The Year 8 Drama curriculum is broken into three main areas of explorative work. In the winter term, pupils discover ways that drama skills can be used in the wider world and explore debating skills, voice-over work for animation, communication for radio, interview techniques and presentation skills. The key performance skills covered are voice, speech, movement, and gesture. In the spring term, pupils work towards the realisation of a devised piece of theatre aimed at a specific target audience. Storytelling and narration skills are developed through the rehearsal process of staging a range of children’s literature. This is coupled with an opportunity to lead a small group in a workshop environment to develop confidence and to determine leadership potential. In the summer term, pupils explore a full play, which allows them to stage extracts and utilise a range of theatrical conventions and page-to-stage techniques. The key performance skills covered are characterisation, effective use of stage space and understanding proxemics.
The Year 9 Drama curriculum is broken into three main areas of explorative work. In the winter term, pupils explore a contemporised play text from the ancient Greek theatrical canon. There is a focus on influential Brechtian techniques and page to stage conventions in preparation for the written paper at GCSE. In the spring term, pupils explore the theatrical style of naturalism through the rehearsal and production process of selected extracts from contemporary dramas. There is a focus on influential Stanislavskian techniques and page to stage conventions in preparation for scripted exam at GCSE. In the summer term, pupils explore a full play text which is presented as a hybrid of performance styles. There is a focus on the works of influential physical theatre and verbatim theatre companies in preparation for the demands of the devised component at GCSE.
At GCSE, pupils follow the Oxford and Cambridge specification and, in their first component, will have the opportunity to devise original theatre from a stimulus. Pupils can be assessed as either an actor or a designer for this component, and there is associated coursework to support the final performance/design realisation. The second component asks pupils to consider page-to-stage conventions when exploring one full play text. Pupils can again be assessed as either an actor or designer, and there is associated coursework to support the two extract performances/design realisations. The final component is a written exam which asks pupils to explore another full play text and answer short and extended response questions from actor, director, and designer perspectives. There is also an extended response question which asks pupils to reflect on a piece of live theatre they have seen. Across the GCSE qualification, pupils will study two full play texts.
At A Level, pupils continue with the Oxford and Cambridge specification and, in their first component, will be asked to explore a range of influential theatre practitioners and one full play text, and to then realise a devised piece of theatre based on these areas of study. The second component asks pupils to explore another full play text and produce an extended extract for performance. There is associated coursework which supports both these components, and pupils have the option to be assessed as an actor or a designer. The final two components are assessed through written papers. The first asks pupils to explore two full play texts and one shared theme from the actor, director, and designer perspectives, as well as an extended live theatre reflection question. The second asks pupils to explore another full play and deconstruct, annotate, and justify artistic intentions for staging specific extracts of that play. Across the A Level qualification, pupils will study five full play texts.
Drama outside of the classroom:
Whether studying Drama as a chosen subject or just showing a love for acting, theatre-making or backstage work, all students have extensive opportunities to develop their skills and interests in the dramatic arena through the variety of co-curricular activities on offer.
The School produces and performs several productions annually, which include a Junior production for Years 7 & 8, a Senior production for Years 9-13, and a number of Studio theatre productions from exam classes and scholars. Produced and directed by the Drama Department, the productions involve our students from start to finish, including aspects such as costume design and creation, choreography, lighting, and props. Here, the students can use all they have learnt in class, but also all of the skills they have developed during the co-curricular activities, such as the Junior Drama Club and the AshTech, our Technical Theatre Club.
High achievers have the opportunity to take part in producing and directing their own showcases, and our A Level students provide mentorship for aspiring dramatists at our annual primary school workshops. Students also regularly participate in festivals and competitions, with recent success obtained at the Kent and Hastings Festivals. A number of our students have also recently auditioned with the National Theatre.
The School welcomes a number of professional practitioners throughout the year, including the Frantic Assembly Physical Theatre Company and the Stanislavski Experience. Our Drama students enjoy several theatre trips throughout the year too, with recent trips to the National Theatre, Shakespeare’s Globe, and London’s West End. This past year we have taken pupils to see A Christmas Carol at the Old Vic, Hex and The Crucible at the NT, Newsies at the Troubadour Wembley Park, The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time at the Orchard Theatre, and Les Misérables at the Marlowe Theatre. Pupils also have the opportunity to consider Drama and Theatre beyond the school, and we actively seek out open days for pupils to attend for degree courses in Acting, Musical Theatre, Stage Management, Technical Design for Stage and Lighting Design and Operation. These experiences can be hugely aspirational for pupils who are considering a career in the Production or Entertainment industries.
Speech and Drama:
Ashford School employs a full-time Speech and Drama teacher and trains a number of Prep and Senior students each year to participate in the LAMDA exams.
We currently have 49 students across the Prep and Senior school taking LAMDA Acting, Verse and Prose and Public Speaking Exams.

Music
The musical life of Ashford School is vibrant; activities and events centre on Brake Hall, the Octagons (two rehearsal and classroom spaces) and a number of individual and larger classrooms for our lessons.
All students in Key Stage 3 (Years 7, 8 and 9) participate in Music.
The Year 7 Instrumental Scheme offers our Year 7 students the opportunity to try out new instruments in rotation for the year. There are four rotations throughout the year with opportunities available on Brass, Guitar, Strings and Woodwind. With the aim of developing a hands-on experience of playing an instrument and offering students the possibility of studying the instrument formally. There is also a strong emphasis on singing with weekly choirs, Year 7 Singers, and opportunities to perform as a Year group.
In Years 8 and 9, pupils are encouraged to develop performance, composition and analytical skills through a variety of musical genres. Our Music Technology Suite (containing twenty PCs) gives students the tools with which to compose, compile and refine creative projects, utilising MuseScore and StudioOne software. This is an important stepping stone to Music as an option at Key Stage 4 (GCSE).
Music at Key Stage 4 and 5 is an optional study, taught as an examinable subject at GCSE and A Level, using the Edexcel specifications. Our students are taught by qualified and experienced teachers and musicians, and have access to first-class facilities, enabling them to write and perform their own music whilst mastering classics and developing an outstanding knowledge of music and its complexities. Alongside our teachers, we also work closely with our visiting music teachers and our composition teacher to ensure that our pupils are well equipped for the Performance and Compositions components of both A Level and GCSE Music.
Music is an all-inclusive department and we welcome all styles of music and ability as well as encourage pupils to take leadership of their own ensembles.
Music beyond the Classroom
Music is not only an integral part of the curriculum at Ashford School but is also an activity that enhances and enriches the co-curricular life of our students. Opportunities for performance are extensive, with a full programme of concerts, recitals and other events taking place throughout the year. As part of our One School policy, we also work with Ashford Prep School’s musical team to collaborate on high-level musical events (in 2023 we performed Vivaldi’s Gloria RV 589 for the 125th Anniversary Celebrations). We offer a broad spectrum of ensembles, clubs, and bands: Orchestra, Training Orchestra, Senior and Junior String Ensembles, Jazz Band, Recorder Ensemble, Flute Choir, Brass Ensemble, Show Choir, Year 7 Singers, Thimann Consort, Boys’ Choir and our talented Chamber Choir. Chamber Choir provide the choral contributions to Commencement and End-of-Term Services, held at St Mary’s Church, Ashford, as well as other concerts and events throughout the year. Chamber Music is encouraged, including piano trios and string ensembles. We are the home of Ashford Youth Jazz Orchestra where membership is open to students from other local schools. AshBash is an event held in the Summer, giving students from across the school to form bands and go wild…
Our Visiting Music teachers provide expert tuition in all orchestral instruments, recorder, guitar (classical, electric and bass), piano, organ (learning on our two-manual Walker instrument in Brake Hall), and voice. Instruments can be hired from the school and the department can also advise on prospective purchase of an instrument.
Each year the Music Department collaborates with the Drama Department on both Junior and Senior productions, including most recently Sister Act in March 2026.
All-Steinway School
– Harry Connick, Jnr.
Ashford School has recently renewed its commitment to Steinway pianos for a further fifteen years, ensuring that our young pianists have the optimum instruments to develop pianism of finesse and assuredness. A new fleet of pianos was delivered in Summer 2023, including a Model-D concert grand piano (our recital instrument, kept in Brake Hall); B-and AS-models are kept in Octagon 2 and the teaching room of the Head of Keyboard; a Steinway upright is complimented by Essex pianos in our practice rooms. We are one of only 25 schools in the UK with Steinway status and proud to have an active relationship with Steinway.

ArtsFest26!
Date Posted: Thursday 09 July 2026
What an incredible fortnight ArtsFest26 was, from beginning with the junior drama collected works seeing some performers on the stage for the very first time all the way through to our final one show metamorphosis performance out on Somerville lawn it was a magnificent demonstration of the creative and performing arts at Ashford School.
One of our ambitious targets for ArtsFest is to have all pupils of the school involved in some way, whether displaying a photo or piece of art in one of our end of year exhibitions, performing a solo in a concert, attending a workshop or taking the lead in a major production. I am thrilled to be getting ever closer to that target, with close to three quarters of the pupils across prep and senior taking part this year, there were two hundred alone on the final night.
In a festival of this scale there are so many highlights, and it feels foolish to list just a few, however I will just dwell on three items.
To put on a festival on this scale is no easy feat. The school is indebted to the goodwill, expertise and enthusiasm of its staff who choreographed, directed, advised, accompanied, and drove the festival creatively. Without them it would not be possible to end the year on such a high.
To the performers, thank you for your confidence, creativity, and good humour in producing such memorable performances and pieces of art.
Thank you to all who attended, I am sure many of you felt like you spent two weeks back at school. It was lovely to welcome so many people onsite and you were all lovely supportive audiences.
Here’s to ArtsFest 27!

Ashford School Launches 125th Anniversary Celebrations in Style!
Date Posted: Friday 31 March 2023
Following months of intense rehearsals and planning, the Ashford School community came together to entertain over 200 guests at a sell-out Celebration Concert, which saw us launch our 125th anniversary in style!
Our Music Department has a particularly poignant role to play in honouring our rich and fascinating heritage. The concert looked forward to the bright future of music at Ashford School, whilst also taking pause to reflect upon the important traditions of years gone by.
Performances during the first half of the night included:
The second half featured the Senior & Training Orchestra uniting to perform an arrangement of Childhood School Hymns, arranged by two of our Sixth Form students, Tom R & Will W. Hugely clever and entertaining, tunes featured in this compilation included favourites such as ‘Sing Hosanna’, ‘All Things Bright and Beautiful’ and ‘One More Step Along the World we Go’!
This was followed by the grand finale and highlight of the evening – Vivaldi’s Gloria, featuring over 250 musicians including students, parents, grandparents, staff, former staff and members of our alumni. An event for the history books.
Congratulations to all those who participated, and huge thanks to our Music Department staff, without whom this event would not have been possible.
We look forward to continuing the 125th anniversary celebrations throughout the year and very much welcome as many guests to join us at any one of our upcoming events. For further information and a list of events, please click here.

Bursaries and Assistance
Ashford School offers a number of financial assistance options for families who meet the criteria.
Scholarships may be supplemented by means-tested bursaries to enable students to attend the school where their parents might not otherwise be able to afford the fees. Applications are invited at 11+ (Year 7), 13+ (Year 9) and 16+ (Year 12) only and awards take into account both parents’ income and assets. The level of assistance varies according to individual circumstances. In exceptional cases a bursary may be awarded to a high performing pupil who is not in receipt of a scholarship.
For pupils applying for a boarding place, the bursary award is applied to the day tuition proportion of the boarding fee only; the proportion of the fee which pays for boarding accommodation and associated costs has to be paid in full.
Bursaries are made available by the School and by The Ashford School Foundation and are subject to eligibility criteria and terms and conditions. To make an enquiry about eligibility for a Bursary, please contact our admissions team by email.
Bursary applications are assessed by a third party company called Bursary Administration Limited (BAL). BAL are a specialist company who operate across the UK, working alongside a large number of Independent Schools.
It is important to note that the School only has a limited amount of funds to be able to dedicate to financial assistance in any one year and therefore, even though you may qualify for bursary, there is no guarantee that a bursary will be awarded, or that we will be able to award the level of financial assistance required in order to be able to afford the school fees.
Bursaries are reviewed on an annual basis and the level of assistance is adjusted according to changes in your financial circumstances.
The Ashford School Foundation is a charity which provides financial support to a small number of students. This support is provided on a means tested-basis and is normally in the region of 10% of the day tuition fee.
It is possible to be awarded a scholarship in addition to a bursary and support provided by the Ashford School Foundation.
These are available to the children of clergy and take into account the joint income of parents. They are open to 11-18 year olds and are normally held by Anglican clergy although we consider requests from other Christian denominations.
Open to children aged 3-18, we offer a 5% discount to the first sibling, 10% to the second and subsequent siblings who are simultaneously enrolled. Families of four or more children should make individual enquiries.
Open to children aged 10-18, this award offers a 20% discount per child on the boarding fee. It is offered to children of serving Forces personnel who are in receipt of the Continuity of Education Allowance (CEA).
Open to children aged 10-18, a discount is available on the boarding fee for children whose parents are employed by the FCO and in reciept of the Continuity of Education Allowance (CEA).

Partnerships and Community
Ashford School is committed to working with local, national, and international organisations, charities, and educational establishments with a mission to raise aspiration by providing opportunities and experiences for young people. We firmly believe that this work holds significant educational value for our students, staff, and other stakeholders as well as those partners who we are working alongside.
Through our partnership work we hope to foster a sense of leadership and service amongst Ashford School pupils, provide collaboration and professional development of our staff while experiencing a greater connection to our local community.
We have three primary areas of focus:
Educational Partnerships
Charity and Community Service

Dover Lifeguards Swim Club (DLGC)
Ashford School is delighted to announce a new partnership with Dover Lifeguards Swim Club (DLGC). This collaboration marks an exciting step forward in enhancing the training, competitive opportunities and long-term development of our swimmers.
Through this partnership, Ashford School swimmers will benefit from access to DLGC’s Swim England affiliations, competitive pathways and expert coaching oversight, while continuing to train within the school’s high-quality facilities during term time. Pupils will compete under the DLGC name at Swim England-affiliated galas, with a jointly-supported competition structure ensuring all swimmers have clear pathways to progress.
We are also pleased to welcome DLGC Head Coach, Dan Cross, who will begin working formally with Ashford School to design training programmes, lead coaching sessions and collaborate closely with our excellent school-based coaching team.
Community Learn to Swim
Our Community Learn to Swim programme provides a vital service to the local Ashford community and operates seven days a week. Our knowledgeable, experienced, and well qualified staff provide a broad offer to young swimmers and adults across our two sites, East Hill, and Great Chart.
We coordinate curriculum swimming for several local primary schools (20 in 2023/24) supporting hundreds (800 in 2023/24) of students through their national curriculum levels.
Our Adult and Child lessons are specifically designed for babies through to children aged 3 and follow the Swim England Discovery Duckling Framework.
Early evening and weekend small group lessons support over 1000 swimmers every week
Weekly adult swimming lessons support all levels of ability from beginners through to athletes in training.
Further information via learntoswim@ashfordschool.co.uk
Led by our Chemistry Ambassadors you will take part in a range of exciting experiments in our specialist science laboratories. Workshops have been created for year 5 pupils and are designed to provide exposure to experimental science.
Led by our Maths department and senior students the ‘Maths Academy’ is a series of academic enrichment workshops aimed at pupils in Year 5 and/or 6.
Year 12 A level students have planned a series of workshops designed to engage and challenge KS2 pupils.
Ashford Youth Jazz Orchestra
The Ashford Youth Jazz Orchestra or AYJO as they are more commonly known, have recently celebrated their 40th anniversary. A jazz band featuring the very best musicians from the area perform regularly in the community at private events and local festivals.
Further information from tvafidis@ashfordschool.co.uk
Ashford Youth Theatre Company
The Ashford Youth Theatre Company are delighted to be part of ‘Connections’ the National Theatres annual nationwide youth festival. Performers from three schools; Ashford, The North and Wye School join forces to perform a brand-new play commissioned by the festival every year.
For further information and to be part of the Ashford Youth Theatre Company please contact mhornsey@ashfordschool.co.uk
Combined Cadet Force
The Combined Cadet Force (CCF) is a youth organisation, sponsored by the Ministry of Defence (MOD), which operates in schools. Its aim is to “provide a disciplined organisation in a school so that students may develop powers of leadership by means of training to promote the qualities of responsibility, self-reliance, resourcefulness, endurance and perseverance”.
Ashford School, Wye School and Chilmington Green CCF is a joint section. It is open to all Year 8-13 students and gives pupils opportunities outside of their comfort zones but in a professional and safe environment. Being a member the CCF will give cadets many opportunities to try new skills, life skills ranging from gliding to receiving an Emergency First Aid at Work certificate.
Mid Kent Junior Dance Festival
Launching in 2025 we are delighted to be founders of the Mid Kent Junior Dance Festival, providing learning and performance opportunities to young aspiring dancers. The inaugural event will see workshops coordinated and delivered by Irena Cuteric of Boy Blue Entertainment.
FareShare Kent and the Ashford Family Foodbank
Ashford School has long established partnership with FareShare Kent and the Ashford Family Foodbank. Spearheaded by Reverand Richard Bellamy, pupil leadership in supporting this vital work has increased year on year.
In 2023 Year 12 pupils led the harvest donation campaign which you can read about here.
This Year, prefects Emily & Vanessa, inspired by their time volunteering in the FareShare warehouse, have, alongside their peers taken part in a food glean on a local farm, made a short documentary film, and presented to the school about the continued need for support.
Each year our four school houses are allocated one ‘house day’ to raise money for their nominated charity. This year the following charities are being supported.

Art
In order to be truly creative, students need to feel safe in their environment. They need to be allowed to make mistakes; they need to be taught the rules and then be free to break the rules.
Only then can we truly teach our students to be exceptionally creative. At Ashford School, our Art department trains pupils from Year 7 upwards to think independently and to be freely creative, therefore developing key skills that students need for their future at university and beyond.
The aim for the department is that, whilst teaching the fundamental skills of drawing and old master painting techniques, we remain highly innovative and contemporary, offering various forms of new media, including green screen, full Adobe Creative Suite, film and animation. Our Art department is acknowledged as one of the very best because it encourages all students to step outside their comfort zone and be adventurous learners in a truly supportive environment. All students are taught the fundamental skills of observational drawing as well as experimenting with a huge array of artistic media – from digital imaging software for green screens, to ceramics, intaglio printing, reduction block printing, screen printing, various forms of textile techniques, dark room and digital photography.
At GCSE, our students participate in workshops that focus on many of the above media. Students are then free to specialise within their chosen areas in year 11. At A level, students learn on a foundation-style course, studying all mediums, under the guidance of three qualified teachers, before being allowed to focus their practise in Year 13.
The art department and its students benefit from a fantastic full-time Art technician who holds a Masters in Fine Art. Our technician is on hand to help and enable ambitious and unusual projects come to life. More recently, these projects have included a mirrored maze exam piece that included sound.
The department also regularly organises student trips to London and surrounding areas for the lower years. Recent GCSE and A Level trips have included residential art tours to Edinburgh, Rome, Madrid, Berlin and Florence.
Outside of the classroom, students have the opportunity to participate in a changing programme of art-focussed co-curricular clubs, which have included photography, graphic art, animation, ceramics, and Art for wellbeing. The School’s own Artist in Residence is also on-hand, allowing the students to talk to and work alongside a professional artist. In recent years, our students have worked alongside and exhibited with an animator, an installation artist, a photographer, a painter and a ceramicist.
The students also benefit from the experienced body of Art staff, who are all highly specialised and are artists within their own right. In recent years, the department staff have showcased their work at their own exhibition to allow students and parents to see their teacher’s passion for the subject.

Pre-Senior Baccalaureate
Pre-Senior Baccalaureate (PSB) at Ashford Prep School
The PSB (Pre-Senior Baccalaureate) is a framework of study that aims to prepare children for the challenges of life as young adults academically, personally, socially, culturally and spiritually. It does so by actively developing and tracking knowledge, skills and attitudes. The PSB is about challenging perceptions of school and developing a love of learning. This is best achieved by children developing a clear understanding of their skills and their areas for development.
At the heart of the PSB are the core skills.
By focusing on the core skills children are best equipped to deal with challenges and provides an opportunity to hone skills that will serve them well later in life – how to be present, how to collaborate, how to be a leader, how to be more independent, how to think out of the box.
The PSB helps our pupils leave Ashford Prep School with a much clearer awareness of their strengths, skills and learning habits.
For further information please see our PSB booklet above or visit the PSB website.

Academic Scholars Programme
Our academic scholars have access to a rigorous package of stretch and support to ensure that they make the very best not only of their award, but of their academic experience at the School.
The central pillars of this are as follows:
Mentoring
Our mentoring programme exists to ensure that all scholars are fully supported through academic life. Each lower and middle school scholar is assigned a dedicated mentor from the staff body who meets them on a half-termly basis to discuss progress, challenges and points for development. These sessions are used as a springboard for academic discussion, promotion of wider reading and exposure to new ideas. In addition, we operate a less formal student mentoring programme, whereby our senior Sixth Form are trained to oversee the progress, attainment and engagement of their younger counterparts. All mentoring is overseen by Mrs Ndongong, Assistant Head (Academic Performance, Sixth Form Lead), who also acts as a lead mentor for Sixth Form academic scholars.
Octagon Lecture Series
Our Octagon Lecture Series, a bespoke programme of talks, exists to push students’ perception of and exposure to different subject disciplines. This runs alongside our wider scheme of department-led enrichment events, such as the Humanities Twilight talks. As part of the Octagon Lecture Series, representatives of each faculty deliver lunchtime talks and host discussions that look at an obscure or unusual element linked to their subject specialism, to take students beyond the parameters of the curriculum. These are delivered on a half-termly basis and are compulsory for all scholars.
Teas and socials
Scholars’ Society Teas are held on a termly basis. All academic scholars are treated to a year-group meet-up with teas, hot chocolate and pastries served. From there, they participate in a briefing, activity or social time. These sessions build on the mentoring programme and encourage socialisation, cross-pollination of ideas, debate, exchange and cohesion as a year group.
Recognition
All academic scholars receive a badge recognising their achievement and status. They also have a dedicated Scholars’ Noticeboard in the library. As well as showing who the scholars are, this displays information on upcoming events, talks, articles, podcasts and exhibitions.
At Ashford School, we have high expectations of academic scholars. The scholarship programme offers the opportunity to set the tone for academic excellence. Accordingly, scholars are expected to participate fully in the programme and act as role models for what hard work, high achievement and effective study skills look like at Ashford School.
Head of Academic Scholars
Student Leadership is an essential cornerstone of the Scholars’ programme, and every year the schedule is overseen by a Senior member of the Upper Sixth. The Head of Academic Scholars coordinates the mentoring scheme, and occupies the role as student ambassador for all award holders. This can range from providing support, delivering lectures to setting the annual agenda. We are extremely proud that our programme is, to a great extent, generated by the students for the students. This outstanding effort (and fierce competition) year on year, is instrumental in ensuring the success and vitality of the programme.

The Somerville Library
With over 13,000 fiction and non-fiction titles, Ashford Senior School’s Somerville Library is a learning hub for all year groups.
Located at the centre of the School campus, it spans three floors, with a designated Sixth Form Study Area on the upper tier, and private study and quiet reading zones for all year groups on the ground and first floors. In these areas students can also access computers, newspapers, magazines and academic journals.
To support our Learning Habits and to encourage independent learning, book displays and reading lists both reinforce and extend the academic content taught across faculties. The online catalogue is regularly updated and pupils are able to access nearly 2000 e-books. Help from the Librarians is also on offer to all year groups when sourcing texts to support homework, project work or research tasks. Assistance is available for those pupils who are following EPQ and CREST Awards, and Study Skills sessions take place each year on research sources and materials, as well as how to use referencing in essays.
Year 7 pupils attend library induction sessions in September of each academic year. Our Librarians also invite both day pupils and boarders to take part in reading initiatives to celebrate World Book Day and National Poetry Day, or to meet visiting authors when they speak at the School.

Pastoral Care at the Senior School
At Ashford School we aim to create a supportive environment where the wellbeing of the child is paramount.
We believe that happiness breeds success, and therefore we are dedicated to ensuring that all pupils feel safe, cared for and happy. We listen, we notice and we communicate.
We have a robust pastoral structure to ensure that every child feels fully supported and knows where to turn.
Each child belongs to a form, which is looked after by a form tutor and is made up of students within their year. Form Tutors have a pivotal role in establishing and maintaining the ethos, style and high expectations of the School and in communicating these to the students in their care. They are key members of the staff team within the Year group structure and, as the person with the most regular contact with their tutor group (twice daily), tutors use their tutee contact time to develop full knowledge of each of their tutees.
The form tutor is the main point of contact for parents, guardians and pupils, and all contact details are provided to parents at the beginning of each academic year.
As from September 2022, the pastoral structure of the School changed. We moved away from the traditional House system and have adopted the Year group system instead. We have our pupils’ best interests at heart when making this decision and the rationale for this new approach is as follows:
The current Heads of Year are:
The Assistant Head oversees issues relating to whole year groups, such as academic tracking, GCSE and A-Level options and cross-Year pastoral matters. They are also a member of the Safeguarding Team.
The current Assistant Head is Mr John Curry.
The Deputy Head is responsible for the overall wellbeing and safeguarding of the whole school.
A former pupil, Nicky Timms returned to Ashford School in 2007 to teach Maths. Since then, she has progressed through the School, reaching Deputy Head Pastoral in September 2016, and Deputy Head in 2021. Along the way, she has experienced various roles within leadership including Director of Co-Curricular Activities, Director of Years 9-11 and Assistant House Parent, thoroughly enjoying the challenges posed by each new role.
Being Deputy Head has further strengthened Nicky’s belief in, and appreciation of, the huge team effort that goes into supporting every child at Ashford School.
Our Health and Wellbeing Centre offers a holistic approach to the physical, psychological and spiritual health and wellbeing of every child at Ashford School. It is based at the top of the School campus and is open to pupils every day between 08:00 and 17:00, plus a nurse is on-call overnight.
The School is fortunate enough to have access to the expertise of four nurses, a School Doctor and our Wellbeing Team. There are two rooms within the Health and Wellbeing Centre available for students who are too unwell to attend lessons, as well as 2 treatment rooms. There is also the Rainbow Room which is used for time out, support work, meetings and drop in sessions; the Wellbeing studio which is used for yoga and mindfulness sessions; and 2 counselling rooms. Within the centre there is also the Reflection room where the School Chaplain can be found.
The Wellbeing Team is based in the Health and Wellbeing Centre. The Wellbeing space offers 2 counselling rooms and a large mindfulness studio, as well as having access to the Rainbow Room.
Ashford School Chaplaincy
Chaplaincy forms an integral part of the commitment of Ashford School to the wellbeing of everyone, regardless of any or no affiliation to a faith tradition and is always committed to a welcoming and non-judgmental approach.
The chaplain is available to listen in confidence* to anyone in the school community. Having time to explain what we think and how we feel forms part of our basic human dignity. All of us will experience times or seasons in our lives when we wrestle with questions about faith as we develop and as our circumstances change. The chaplain is available to offer support and pastoral care to any member of the school community, not only to those who identify with faith traditions.
Ashford Senior School continues a very long and enriching association with St Mary’s Church in Ashford town centre, and with St Mary’s Great Chart for the Prep School. As a learning community, commencement, and end of term services, as well as other times and seasons throughout the year, provide a helpful framework of gathering to express gratitude and to seek help. Moments of quiet reflection are integral to our services and valued by students and staff alike.
*Safeguarding concerns will be passed to the Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL).
Next to the Chaplain’s office, the Quiet Room in the Wellbeing Centre, is a special place free from distraction, where anyone can simply relax and enjoy a quiet space. Excellent resources are available to help explore faith through a range of traditions in a comfortable and calm setting. The chaplain is always happy to discuss questions about faith, spirituality, or religious practice. From 1pm to 1:15pm the Quiet Room is used by students wishing to pray or meditate as part of their devotional life.
The Chaplain is normally at the Prep School on Monday mornings and the Senior School on Wednesdays & Fridays, but can also be available on other days. Knowing that someone is praying for us is very positive and reassuring. Speak to the Chaplain if you would value prayer.
